lead.title: AMD launches Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 with 192GB unified memory - up to 160GB addressable as VRAM
lead.summary: At its IFA 2026 opening keynote AMD commercially launched the Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 series, whose single LPDDR5X-8533 pool of up to 192GB (around 273 GB/s) lets the integrated Radeon 8060S iGPU map up to 160GB as VRAM - on paper enough to hold quantized 300B-parameter models on a desk with no discrete GPU and no cloud. Commercial systems from HP and Lenovo are targeted for Q3 2026; the 192GB SKU's tight SK Hynix LPDDR5X supply remains the open question.

top_stories.title: NVIDIA: new llama.cpp and vLLM optimizations lift local LLM throughput up to 1.9x on RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000 and DGX Spark
top_stories.summary: New XQA attention kernels in FlashInfer deliver up to 1.9x throughput (Qwen3.6-35B on an RTX 5090), with 1.2x on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and 1.4x on a dual DGX Spark cluster; the gains reach users through llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio and Ollama.

top_stories.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6, codenamed 'Astra', reported as its most advanced model yet
top_stories.summary: Bloomberg Technology hands-on coverage frames the release as a possible step toward general-purpose capability; local-AI relevance is indirect but the release dominates the weekend's AI news.

items.title: Why Gated DeltaNet survives 4-bit quantization: NVFP4 W4A4 for the recurrent half of a hybrid 27B LLM
items.summary: Quantizes all 496 Gated DeltaNet layers of the hybrid 27B Qwen3.8-27B to NVFP4 W4A4, including the decay and write-strength gates previously kept at 8/16-bit, and matches BF16 within seed noise across perplexity, MMLU-Pro, GSM8K, AIME'25, GPQA-Diamond and RULER to 64K tokens - disproving the community intuition that recurrent-state errors accumulate fatally under low precision.

items.title: Random attention: scored token selection adds almost nothing to KV cache eviction
items.summary: Salesforce AI Research shows that evicting uniformly at random per attention head, while keeping the prompt, matches the strongest prior evictor across four models and six reasoning tasks while serving 32-43% higher throughput in vLLM deployment.

items.title: Rethinking on-policy distillation II: one training example is enough to go far
items.summary: On-policy distillation on a single query keeps improving for hundreds of steps and recovers most of full-data OPD's gain across task domains and model families, making distillation feasible at the data-minimal limit.

items.title: Hardware-aware FP4 FlashAttention-4 maps attention scores straight to FP4 probabilities
items.summary: Reaches up to 2.13x the BF16 forward throughput on an NVIDIA GB200 (Blackwell) by feeding the forward quantization directly into the backward pass with FP8 gradient operators, addressing the finding that FP4 tensor cores alone do not speed up attention once softmax conversion dominates.

items.title: VestigeKV: the NoPE-MLA KV cache carries its own eviction signal in a vestigial branch
items.summary: On Kimi Linear, attention-observed selectors like H2O and SnapKV collapse on needle retrieval; VestigeKV evicts using the query-independent signal already present in the 64-dimensional decoupled RoPE branch, reading 11% of each row to partition the cache before future queries exist.

items.title: Unlocking lossless speedups in LLMs via discrete diffusion
items.summary: Diffusion-augmented LLMs keep the autoregressive distribution but use lightweight diffusion weights to draw multiple tokens in parallel from it, targeting the sequential-generation bottleneck with lossless decoding speedups.

items.title: IFM releases K2 Horizon: six fully open models (0.9B-375B) with weights, code and training data
items.summary: The Institute of Foundation Models opens everything - weights, code, training data, recipes and evaluations - across a fleet from 0.9B to 375B, with diffusion distillation for roughly 3x faster inference and a Mixture-of-Value-Attention 36B-A4B model that reportedly beats MoE models up to 15x its size; the 36B-A4B GGUF checkpoints landed on the Hub yesterday.

items.title: FastVideo publishes FastH3, a 4-step 35B text-to-video preview
items.summary: A 35B text-to-video model whose name indicates a four-step generation path, VSA attention and a data-free training route; the card appeared yesterday and is already trending on the Hub - a fast pipeline to watch for local video synthesis on consumer GPUs.

items.title: Spark-X2.5-4B and 1.7B: claimed first edge models with native 1M-token context
items.summary: XHToken ships weights, code and deployment docs for a 4B and a 1.7B model with a native 1M-token window and vLLM/SGLang quickstart paths; the card is trending this weekend and drew a YouTube benchmark review questioning superiority over Gemma 4 and Qwen.

items.title: llama.cpp ships v0.4.0, its second semver-stable release
items.summary: Adds initial Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B support, on-demand lazy tensor reading (--lazy-mode), per-slot server context limits, video-input options, per-layer expert routing/FFN, an n-gram history lookup and quantizer RAM caps / row-slab streaming to cut peak memory during load; the ggml bump to 0.23.0 comes along too.

items.title: ggml v0.23.0 lands sparse attention, async RPC and an Apple RDMA transport
items.summary: The tensor backend underneath llama.cpp gains scheduling APIs for sparse attention (n_kv_max K/V masks), asynchronous execution and allocation-dependency tracking, plus an RPC protocol bump to 6.0.0 with an Apple RDMA transport and broad correctness work across CPU, GPU and accelerator backends.

items.title: Show HN: Sageling runs Qwen 3.5 9B in-process on Apple Silicon via MLX
items.summary: A free Apple-Silicon-only assistant that keeps files, conversations and memories on the Mac by running a roughly 8 GB Qwen model fully in-process through MLX; targets non-developers with skill briefs for transcription, notes and document grading and needs 16 GB+ RAM on macOS 13 or later.

items.title: Show HN: Moadim is a local, cron-free scheduler daemon for coding agents
items.summary: A Rust daemon that pairs a prompt, a schedule and an agent (Claude, Codex, Hermes, NanoClaw or Pi), launches each tick in an isolated tmux session with a watchdog, and exposes the loops over a UI, a REST API with an OpenAPI/Swagger schema and an MCP endpoint; installs as a launchd or systemd service.

items.title: Show HN: Personal Context MCP puts accounts, memory and skills behind one self-hostable endpoint
items.summary: Lanes Link is a free, open-source, self-hostable MCP server that exposes a user's accounts, memory and skills via Access Profiles to every agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, OpenCode) with 100+ provider connectors - the consumer-side counterpart to hosted MCP gateways.

items.title: NVIDIA launches PAIR beta: a Personal AI Router that pools home PCs for local LLM inference
items.summary: A free open-source tool that discovers machines on the home network running Ollama or LM Studio and distributes local AI/agent inference requests across them by real-time device capacity, with mTLS-encrypted traffic between nodes; the beta supports Windows, Linux and macOS (Apple M4 or newer) and is positioned for households with a gaming PC plus a laptop.

items.title: Ollama 0.33.3 brings multimodal Gemma 4 (images and audio) to Apple Silicon's MLX engine
items.summary: On Apple Silicon, Gemma 4 now handles image and audio input on the MLX engine without a CUDA GPU; the release also reports cached prompt tokens separately and honors GGUF-defined default parameters, and the v0.34.0 line has opened with two release candidates carrying a ChatGPT Desktop integration.

items.title: Lenovo ThinkCentre X Ultra: 1.6-liter Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 mini PC with 128GB unified memory, clusterable four-deep to 512GB
items.summary: At IFA 2026 Lenovo announced a 1.6L box built around AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 (16 Zen 5 cores, Radeon 8060S iGPU, about 55 TOPS NPU) with up to 128GB of unified LPDDR5X, starting at $3,699 and shipping November 2026; up to four units can pool as much as 512GB of coherent memory, DGX-Spark-class capacity at roughly 50% less cost per box.

items.title: AMD unveils Threadripper Halo Station at IFA: a liquid-cooled workstation targeting trillion-parameter local inference
items.summary: Built on a 96-core Threadripper Pro 9995WX with support for up to four enterprise MI350P GPUs, aimed at running models over 1 trillion parameters locally as an alternative to cloud towers; pricing and availability are still undisclosed.

items.title: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney compares the component shortage to the 1983 video game crash; expects 3+ more years of tight memory supply
items.summary: Sweeney says AI data-center demand is outbidding entertainment for DRAM and storage, with RAM and SSD prices quadrupling and no meaningful relief for at least three years absent new fabs - extending the memory-cost squeeze that keeps 24GB+ VRAM cards and high-unified-memory mini PCs far above launch pricing for homelab builders.

items.title: Malaysia's APU opens first university lab powered by NVIDIA DGX Spark, serving up to 200B-parameter models locally
items.summary: The Asia Pacific University launched a facility built on NVIDIA's 128GB GB10 Grace Blackwell DGX Spark, described as Malaysia's first university lab able to process AI models up to 200 billion parameters on-prem, giving students direct local inference without cloud dependencies.
